description: We didn't find these at a park but in town. My mother who is a volunteer for the Arlington P.D. wanted to take me to the Police Training Academy because she has been taking a class there the same day I have Master Naturalist meetings. She saiid she wanted me to see the spiders and that was what we did Easter Sunday. Oh my goodness there were big spiders everywhere. It reminded me so much of an episode from Doctor Who or Indiana Jones. These spiders are all over the wall off the station and it was kind of cool but creepy but in a fun way. These were pretty much all the same spiders. These guys were heavily patterned and had colors of gray and black and tan. Some of their webs were huge and the walls are covered in insect debris and mangled cobwebs. It reminded me so much of halloween decor except this decor was alive and moving. This place is a death trap for any insects that come to it. I have a photo of one off the large webs Just to show you what it looks like. I have never seen so many spiders at one time that were web weavers. I have been among dozens of Wolf Spiders of all sizes and have seen groups of different insects. This place could be an Arachnophobes worst nightmare. The whole wall was crawling. It was so weird. They didn't seem to mind to each other.

description: Captured this morning for a “school pic” 😲 and released.

PHYLUM ARTHROPODA (4/4)
Found against a door window on a busy building. Habitat was humid and it was dark except for artificial light. Temperature was in the high 70s. The web, being in a doorway, would have been disturbed frequently.
 I notice rather than choosing a corner of the door or window, let alone a nearby bush, the specimen opted to form its web in the middle of the window where light shone through the glass. The specimen continued to form the web despite the opening and closing of the door. 
 I wonder why this specimen chose such a disrupted place for its web, and I wonder if its placement was intended to trap prey that was attracted to the light from inside the window.
 This reminds me of the predator adaptations we discussed in class such as tricking or startling in order to catch prey. This could be a coevolved species, given its potential connection to prey tendencies.
